heroCommands.comment: Run goose as an agent behind your app

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: goose is an open-source, general-purpose AI agent for coding, research, writing, automation and data analysis. You use it as a desktop app or from the terminal, connect tools through MCP, and pick from over 85 model providers or local models.
sixtySeconds.problem: Many AI agents are tied to one vendor or one interface. goose is open, runs on your machine, works with many model providers and can also be embedded in your own application as its agent backend.
whoFor: Developers who want an open-source coding agent
People automating research, writing or data tasks
Builders embedding an agent in their own app
Rust developers building custom agents with oi-kit
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a vendor-neutral agent with a desktop app, CLI and MCP support, governed by the Agentic AI Foundation at the Linux Foundation.
requirements: A model provider account (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini and more) or a local model

overview: This repository holds two things: goose, a complete agent with a desktop app and CLI, and oi-kit, the reusable Rust components goose is built from. goose is part of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) at the Linux Foundation.

goose connects tools and data through the Model Context Protocol and works with over 85 providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter and Amazon Bedrock. It can also load local models directly without a separate model server.

Running goose acp starts it as a subprocess speaking the Agent Client Protocol, so your own app can send prompts and receive streamed responses, tool activity and permission requests. oi-kit is in alpha; Rust exposes the full runtime, and Python and Kotlin bindings cover providers, streaming and compaction.
